content: 1. The concurrent administration of a YP1A2 inhibitor may lead to increased plasma concentrations of bendamustine. 2. Bosentan reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be diminished; therefore, alternative or nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 3. Brigatinib decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with hormonal contraceptives may reduce their efficacy. Women should use effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last dose of brigatinib. 4. Butabarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; alternative or nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 5. Ethinylestradiol increases caffeine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 6. Calaspargase pegol may interact indirectly with oral contraceptives, reducing their efficacy. Non-oral contraceptive methods are recommended for women of childbearing potential. 7. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norgestimate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative contraceptive methods should be used during co-administration and for 28 days after discontinuation. 8. Ethinylestradiol increases carbamazepine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; alternative or nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 9. Certain antibiotics (e.g., cefaclor, cefadroxil, cefazolin, cefdinir, cefepime, cefixime, cefotaxime, cefprozil, ceftazidime, ceftibuten, cefuroxime, cephalexin, chloramphenicol, ciprofloxacin, clindamycin) may reduce ethinylestradiol levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of hormones and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Ceritinib increases ethinylestradiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Clobazam decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norgestimate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 12. Ethinylestradiol increases clomipramine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. This may lead to increased serum concentrations of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) and potential adverse effects. 13. Ethinylestradiol increases clonazepam levels or effects by decreasing its metabolism. It may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines undergoing oxidation, increasing their serum concentrations. 14. Conivaptan increases ethinylestradiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs are recommended. 15. Cyclophosphamide increases ethinylestradiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 16. Ethinylestradiol increases cyclosporine levels by an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Dabrafenib decreases ethinylestradiol levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative contraceptive methods should be considered. 18. Danazol increases ethinylestradiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 19. Darunavir decreases ethinylestradiol levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 20. Dexamethasone decreases ethinylestradiol levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 21. Ethinylestradiol increases diazepam levels or effects by decreasing its metabolism. It may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines undergoing oxidation, increasing their serum concentrations. 22. Dicloxacillin decreases ethinylestradiol levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of hormones and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Ethinylestradiol increases dosulepin and doxepin levels or effects by inhibiting oxidative metabolism of TCAs. This may lead to increased serum concentrations and potential adverse effects. 24. Doxycycline decreases ethinylestradiol levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of hormones and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Drospirenone increases ethinylestradiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 26. Ethinylestradiol increases duloxetine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 27. Efavirenz decreases ethinylestradiol levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 28. Elafibranor decreases ethinylestradiol levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods or additional barrier methods are recommended during treatment and for at least 3 weeks after the last dose. 29. Elagolix decreases ethinylestradiol levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Estrogen-containing contraceptives may reduce elagolix efficacy. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended during treatment and for 1 week after discontinuation. 30. Ethinylestradiol increases eltrombopag levels or effects by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 31. Elvitegravir decreases ethinylestradiol levels or effects by an unknown mechanism. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 32. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases ethinylestradiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates associated with serious or life-threatening events. 33. Enasidenib increases ethinylestradiol levels or effects by inhibiting OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP substrates. Co-administration with sensitive substrates is not recommended.
